article.title: 完形填空 · 在社交不足与社交透支之间找到平衡
article.context: 文章讨论社交生活的适度原则：独处过多会带来孤独与脱节，社交过度又可能造成倦怠；更健康的做法是在恢复社交联系的同时，为自己明确留出不社交的休息时间。
rows: Your social life is defined as “the activities you do with other people, for pleasure, when you are not working”.
社交生活被定义为“你在不工作时，为了愉悦而与他人一起进行的活动”。
advance
It’s important to have a social life, but what’s right for one person won’t be right for another.
拥有社交生活很重要，但适合一个人的方式未必适合另一个人。
contrast
Some of us feel energised by spending lots of time with others, whereas some of us may feel drained, even if it’s doing something we enjoy.
有些人与他人长时间相处会感到精力充沛，而另一些人即使参加自己喜欢的活动，也可能因此感到疲惫。
compare
This is why finding a balance in your social life is key.
因此，在社交生活中找到平衡至关重要。
emphasize
Spending too much time on your own, not seeing others, can make you feel lonely and disconnected.
独处太久、很少与人见面，会让你感到孤独，并与他人失去连接。
warning
Loneliness is known to impact on your mental health and contribute to a low mood.
众所周知，孤独会影响心理健康，并使情绪低落。
explain
Anyone can feel lonely at any time.
任何人都可能在任何时候感到孤独。
qualify
This might be especially true if, for example, you are working from home and you are missing out on the usual social conversations that happen in an office.
例如，如果你居家办公，错过了办公室里日常发生的社交交谈，这种孤独感可能尤其明显。
example
Other life changes can trigger periods of loneliness too, such as retirement, changing jobs or becoming a parent.
退休、换工作或成为父母等其他人生变化，也可能引发一段时期的孤独。
explain
It’s important to recognise these feelings of loneliness.
意识到这些孤独感很重要。
emphasize
There are ways to regain a social life, but it can feel overwhelming at first.
重新建立社交生活是有办法的，只是一开始可能让人觉得无从下手。
contrast
It’s a great idea to start by thinking about hobbies you enjoy.
不妨先从想一想自己喜欢的爱好开始。
encourage
You can then find groups and activities related to those where you will be able to meet like-minded people.
随后可以寻找与这些爱好相关的团体和活动，在那里结识志趣相投的人。
sequence
There are groups aimed at new parents, at those who want to try a new sport for the first time, or networking events for those in the same profession to meet up and share ideas.
有些团体面向新手父母，有些面向第一次想尝试某项新运动的人；同一职业的人也可以参加交流活动，见面分享想法。
example
On the other hand, it’s also possible to have too much of a social life.
另一方面，社交生活也可能过量。
contrast
If you feel like you’re always doing something and there is never any space in your calendar for downtime, you could suffer social burnout or social fatigue.
如果你总觉得自己一直在忙各种活动，日程表里从来没有留给放松的空档，就可能出现社交倦怠或社交疲劳。
warning
We all have our own social limit and it’s important to recognise when you’re feeling like it’s all too much.
每个人都有自己的社交上限；当你觉得这一切已经过量时，意识到这一点很重要。
emphasize
Low mood, low energy, irritability and trouble sleeping could all be signs of poor social health.
情绪低落、精力不足、易怒和睡眠困难，都可能是社交健康不佳的迹象。
warning
Make sure you mark out some time in your diary when you’re unavailable for socialising and use this time to relax, rest and recover.
务必在日程中明确划出一段“不参加社交”的时间，用来放松、休息和恢复。
encourage
